### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `25aee63433439ca028574036e36f669276507817` — the merge of head `43d3e41fed67a1ead21d20b0b0666e45f7825175` into base `ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 25aee63433439ca028574036e36f669276507817 && git checkout 25aee63433439ca028574036e36f669276507817
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 43d3e41fed67a1ead21d20b0b0666e45f7825175 && git checkout -B drift-repro ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 && git merge --no-ff 43d3e41fed67a1ead21d20b0b0666e45f7825175

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `43d3e41fed67a1ead21d20b0b0666e45f7825175`

Inputs read: card #34387 (body and all 4 comments), PR #34532 (body, 3-file list, both comments), the net diff of the head against the main it merged (second parent 0e2ead3c; 3 files, 63 insertions, 33 deletions), and the check-runs on the head. Read, not reviewed, on that main: ruling 6909355256 on #34209, `TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE.requiresConfirmation` (packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts), `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY` and the refusal reasons (packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts), `handOffActionConfirmation` and `confirmationRefusalOf` (packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts), `RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER`, `strictToolInput` and the `run_action` registration (packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts), and migration entry `action-requires-confirmation-elicited`. No file in the diff implements or enforces the entry, so the second half of the scope is none; docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets: none moves. The diff changes two string fields (`replacement`, `acceptanceCriteria`) of one `SemanticMigration` entry; `id`, `surface`, `reason` and `relevantWhen` are untouched, so which stacks the entry matches and what any schema accepts are unchanged. Right.
- Public surface: the entry text ships in the `@objectstack/spec` build and is projected by `os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide, so the wording is published. The change is a correction of published prose to the behaviour already on main; no export, key or code is added or removed. Right.
- No generated artefact carries the old sentences: a search of the head tree for the removed phrases finds only release-owned CHANGELOG files and two code comments outside the diff. Right to leave them.
- Gate verdicts are the check-runs on the head. Concluded success: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, both shard planners, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter. Pending when this record was rendered (no verdict taken from them): Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus. No check has concluded failure. This PASS is the contract judgment; the pending checks remain the landing gate's to read.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no

The changeset `.changeset/34387-entry17-confirm-text.md` declares `@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two lines. That matches what the diff publishes: corrected upgrade-guidance prose in one package, no accept set widened or narrowed, no protocol change. Patch is the right level, and the narrowing arm is not owed (the narrowing itself landed with #34358). Check Changeset concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (does landing need a contract-tier record at this head): answered A. The path is on the schema face, and this record is that review.
- Dev out-of-scope finding (the docblock of `recordDeleteConfirmationRefusal` in packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts still says `run_action` takes `confirm: true`): confirmed present on main, and a second comment in packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts carries the same old phrase. Both are internal comments outside this diff with no reader at a public door; no carrier is owed by this PR. The seat may file a tidy card.
- Security findings: none reported, none found. The new text narrows what a caller is told it can do and discloses no mechanism beyond the tool descriptions already served.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff holds no query, id materialisation or join.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/17.tool-requires-confirmation-retired.ts, each claim checked against the ruling, the gate code on main and the guidance entry:

- Who confirms. "a person confirms, never the caller" and "The caller cannot confirm for the person". Ruling: the tools refuse the member, confirmation happens by the person. Guidance: "a person confirms, never the agent". Agrees.
- Elicit. "in the client, when it supports elicitation and the connection can carry the question (accept runs the call; decline, dismissal or no answer in time refuses it with `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`)". Contract step 1 and rule 4 (reasons `declined`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`) and the served `run_action` description say the same. Agrees, word for word with the guidance.
- Hand-off. "the call does not run, it is handed to the person, who approves or rejects it there, and the tool answers `status: 'pending_confirmation'` with a pending id". `handOffActionConfirmation` returns exactly that with the service's `pendingId` and runs nothing. Agrees.
- No service. "refuses it with `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (428) and `details.reason` `no_confirmation_service`, and the person performs the action in the app". The no-service branch builds the refusal through `confirmationRefusalOf` with that reason; `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_STATUS` is 428; the message says to perform the action in the app. Agrees. The entry names the reason where the guidance names only the code; that is an addition the code supports, not a disagreement.
- "Nothing is written before the person approves." Contract rule 2: a call refused or never confirmed may have read its subject and writes nothing. The old sentence "no record was read and none was written" would now be false and is correctly gone, as is "A gate, not a queue: nothing is parked", which a hand-off contradicts.
- Member refusal. "both tools refuse any call that carries the `confirm` member, on every action and whatever its value, so a client sends the call without it". `run_action` and `resume_run` declare no such member and pass `RETIRED_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` to the closed input, which refuses by key before the bridge is called, so the value is never read. Ruling: every action, the client resends without it. Agrees.
- Older runtime parenthesis. It points to `action-requires-confirmation-elicited`, which exists on main and does say how to tell which runtime you run (the changelog line about the hand-off) and that the earlier one still gated on the caller's `confirm: true`. Agrees.
- Bounds. The first bound is the previous text plus `resume_run`, matching bound (1) of the guidance, including the REST `/actions` carve-out and the AI-service-account rule (reason `service_account`, refused at every door). The second bound replaces the retired "unverifiable caller claim" sentence with bound (2) of the guidance (only the declared `true` asks the person; the listing heuristic advises and never gates), which is the contract's rule 1. Agrees.
- `acceptanceCriteria`. The check it offers still holds on every branch: asked and declined, handed off and not approved, or refused with no service, nothing runs on the caller's word, and the call is made without `confirm`. I tried the service-account caller, the HTTP door with an elicitation-capable client, and an accepted elicitation; none makes the stated check destructive or its expected answer wrong.

N1 (nit) — `acceptanceCriteria` says "The person is asked in a client that supports elicitation" without the qualifier the `replacement` field and the guidance carry ("and the connection can carry the question"). Over the Streamable HTTP door such a client is handed off, not asked. The next clause ("the call is otherwise handed to them") covers that case and the criterion's outcome is the same, so correctness and the contract are unaffected. Left as an accepted deviation; a fix would move the head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
